claim: The note says every date from the 11th onward is regular number + にち (nichi), but the book table this lesson teaches prints three irregular dates after the 10th.
evidence: Book WORD POWER: "じゅうよっか 14th ... はつか 20th ... にじゅうよっか 24th". Card note: "Days 1st–10th of the month have irregular readings that must be memorized individually; from the 11th onward the pattern becomes regular: number + にち (nichi, "day")."
fix: Say the 11th onward is regular number + にち except the 14th (じゅうよっか), 20th (はつか) and 24th (にじゅうよっか).

claim: The note says 〜にち names a day of the month from the 11th onward without mentioning the 14th, 20th and 24th, which the book prints without にち.
evidence: Book WORD POWER: "じゅうよっか 14th", "はつか 20th", "にじゅうよっか 24th". Card note: "attaches after a number to name a day of the month (from the 11th onward), e.g. じゅういちにち".
fix: Add "(except the 14th, 20th and 24th)" after "from the 11th onward".

claim: The note names a "まし past-tense pattern", which is not a form; the past ending is ました (mashita).
evidence: Card note: "The まし past-tense pattern from いきました／きました extends to かえります too." Book Exercise V: "スミスさんは ちかてつで うちに かえりました。"
fix: Change "The まし past-tense pattern" to "The ました (mashita) past ending".

claim: The note says Japanese month-then-day is the reverse of the usual English order, but the card English itself gives month then day ("October 9th").
evidence: Card English: "My birthday is October 9th." Card note: "The month comes first and the day second, the reverse of the usual English order." Book Exercise II.B: "8 がつ 19 にち です" (no claim about English order).
fix: Drop the clause about English order, or say month comes before day, as in "October 9th".

claim: The note explains keeping が (ga) as avoiding "a change of subject", which neither the book nor the Lesson 6 が cards say; the book rule is that が follows interrogatives like どの (dono).
evidence: Book L6 GRAMMAR: "が, the subject marker, is used instead of the topic marker は after interrogatives like どれ and どの." Card note: "The answer keeps が (ga) — swapping in は (wa) would make it sound like a change of subject."
fix: Reuse the chapter-6-extras wording: the reply to a どの…が question keeps が, never は.
